The Indian pilot, who managed to unlock the cockpit door of a fly Dubai flight this week
after he was stabbed, is being hailed as a hero for effectively saving the lives of as
many as 182 people on board, NPR's Dia Hadid reports.
The pilot's name is Smith Machar, and Indian TV channels like Republic World and News18
spared no praise for him.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi video called Machar, who is recovering in a Dubai hospital,
and told him the whole country is praying for you.
Machar was stabbed by his co-pilot while on a fly Dubai flight, packed with Israeli nationals.

Dia Hadid, NPR News, Mumbai.
A group of mathematicians is calling for better vetting of new results from artificial intelligence.
As NPR's Jeff Bromfield reports, the push comes after one company claimed a major discovery.
The independent group of mathematicians is calling for AI labs to do more vetting of
discoveries.
They also want them to be presented in a way that a human can understand.
Melanie Matchedwood is with Harvard.
A lot of the AI mathematical output is doing a very bad job of showing and communicating
its work.
The recommendations came after OpenAI claimed to have solved one of the toughest problems
in mathematics using its AI tools.
Some mathematicians, though, are still trying to untangle the AI's poorly-written 166-page
proof to see if it actually found a solution.
Jeff Bromfield, NPR News.
You're listening to NPR.
Researchers say animals may have evolved up to 200 million years before they showed up
on the fossil record, and PR's Ping Wang has more.
The oldest animal fossils are about 550 million years old.
Ross Anderson, a natural historian at Oxford University, says they're mostly shells and
skeletons.
Presumably animals had a history before this, but because the animals then are soft and
squishy, it's actually really hard to get them preserved as fossils.
New analysis by Anderson and his colleagues suggests that animals came long before that
when much of the Earth was a ball of ice.
Looking at evidence from sites around the world, they calculated the maximum age for the origin
of animals back some 750 million years ago.
These were probably sponge-like critters that lived on the seafloor.
While this research doesn't prove animals existed that long ago, Anderson says it gives
them a direction in which to dig for evidence.
The paper is published in the journal Science Advances.
Ping Wang, NPR News.
Scientists in Argentina are trying to find out why unusually high numbers of baby whales
have been washing up dead along the Panagonian coast.
The lead researcher says bacterial infections could be to blame and adds that the bacteria
may be spread by seabirds.
Researchers also are exploring whether warming waters or other environmental changes are
playing a role.
The losses could slow the recovery of the southern right whales, which were once hunted
to the brink of extinction.
I'm Lyndi Kenyon, NPR News, in Washington.
